Let $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, let $U_0$ be unitary, and set $H_0=U_0^*AU_0$. For $j=1,\ldots,m$, suppose

$$H_j=P_j^*(H_{j-1}+E_j+D_j)P_j,$$

where each $P_j$ is unitary, $E_j$ is a local arithmetic perturbation, and $D_j$ is a local deflation perturbation. Then for $U_m=U_0P_1\cdots P_m$ there is a matrix $\Delta$ such that

$$H_m=U_m^*(A+\Delta)U_m,\qquad \|\Delta\|_F\le\sum_{j=1}^m\bigl(\|E_j\|_F+\|D_j\|_F\bigr).$$

The assertion also holds over $\mathbb R$ with orthogonal factors.

Let $F$ be a field, let $m,n,p\in\mathbb N$, and let
$A=(a_{ij})\in M_{m\times n}(F)$ and
$B=(b_{jk})\in M_{n\times p}(F)$. Their **matrix product** is the matrix
$AB\in M_{m\times p}(F)$ whose entries are

$$(AB)_{ik}:=\sum_{j\in n}a_{ij}b_{jk}.$$

The sum is the finite sum in the additive commutative monoid of $F$. If $n=0$,
it is the empty sum, so $AB$ is the zero matrix of shape $m$ by $p$.

The **identity matrix** $I_n\in M_n(F)$ has entry $1$ when $i=j$ and entry $0$
when $i\ne j$. In particular, $I_0$ is the unique empty matrix in $M_0(F)$.

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let
$A=(a_{ij})\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$. The **Frobenius norm** of $A$ is

$$\lVert A\rVert_F\;:=\;\Bigl(\,\sum_{i<m}\sum_{j<n}|a_{ij}|^{2}\Bigr)^{1/2},$$

where $|\cdot|$ is the absolute value on $\mathbb R$
([[def-abs-value]]) for $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ and the modulus on $\mathbb C$
([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]) for
$\mathbb F=\mathbb C$, and the outer power is the nonnegative real square root.

**The displayed quantity is a norm.** Regard $A$ as the element of the
coordinate space $\mathbb F^{mn}$ whose $j+in$-th entry is $a_{ij}$. The
standard coordinate inner product of [[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]
satisfies $\langle A,A\rangle=\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}\overline{a_{ij}}$, which equals
$\sum_{i,j}|a_{ij}|^{2}$ because $z\overline z=|z|^{2}$
([[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]). Thus $\lVert A\rVert_F$ is
exactly the inner-product norm of [[def-inner-product-norm]] evaluated at $A$,
and the three norm axioms hold for $\lVert\cdot\rVert_F$ because they hold for
every inner-product norm. For real matrices the same sum is
$\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}^{2}$, since $|x|^{2}=x^{2}$ for real $x$ by the two cases of
[[def-abs-value]].

The Frobenius norm is the Euclidean norm of the full entry list, not the
largest factor by which the matrix stretches a single vector. It can coincide
with an induced $2$-norm in one-row or one-column cases, but in general it is a
different matrix norm from the induced operator norms used on this page. Its
relation to the spectral norm, its unitary invariance and its singular-value
formula are
[[thm-spectral-and-frobenius-norms-are-unitarily-invariant-with-singular-value-formulas-and-rank-comparison]].

order, $i=n,n-1,\ldots,j+1$, set

triangular in the senses of
[[def-upper-hessenberg-and-real-symmetric-tridiagonal-matrices]] and
[[def-triangular-and-diagonal-matrices-over-a-commutative-ring]]. The outputs are represented by the exact products of

derivations.claim: The triangularisation loops range over finitely many pairs $(i,j)$. For fixed $j$, descending $i$ zeros $B_{i,j}$ without changing already cleared entries below it. The rotations act on rows with indices at least $j$, whose entries in columns less than $j$ are zero by upper triangularity; hence they do not create below-diagonal entries in earlier columns. After all columns, $B$ is upper triangular.

For $j=1$ there are no earlier Hessenberg columns, so the base condition is vacuous. For general $j$, assume every earlier column already has the Hessenberg pattern. Descend through $i$; the left factor zeros $A_{i,j}$. Since $B$ was upper triangular, this left factor can create below-diagonal fill only at $B_{i,i-1}$; the paired right factor zeros that entry. It creates no further below-diagonal entries in $B$, because rows below $i$ are zero in columns $i-1,i$. The right factor does not touch column $j$ because $i-1\ge j+1$, and the left factors preserve all earlier Hessenberg columns, whose entries in rows $i-1,i$ are already zero. Input a regular pencil $(A,B)$ with $A,B\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$,
$n\ge1$, a nonnegative integer sweep budget $N$, and a finite tolerance
$\tau\ge0$. Real input data are embedded in $\mathbb C$. Scalar updates of the
stored matrices use the operationwise model of
[[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]].
Exact unitary Givens factors are retained as products rather than rounded dense
matrices; if a concrete factor computation cannot return such a factor with a
local error certificate, the run keeps its diagnostics and reports
`certificate-inconclusive`.

1. Reduce $(A,B)$ to Hessenberg-triangular form using
[[alg-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-reduction]]. Record each rounded matrix
update's exact local residual $E_j^A,E_j^B$ against its exact left/right
unitary update, and each structural zeroing as a deflation perturbation
$D_j^A,D_j^B$.

2. On each active block $H_{a:b,a:b},T_{a:b,a:b}$, apply the following deflation
tests before a sweep. For $i=a,ldots,b-1$, set $H_{i+1,i}$ to zero when
$$|H_{i+1,i}|\le\tau\bigl(|H_{i,i}|+|H_{i+1,i+1}|\bigr),$$
and record its old value in $D^A$. For $k=a,ldots,b$, set $T_{k,k}$ to zero when
$$|T_{k,k}|\le\tau\bigl(|T_{k-1,k}|+|T_{k,k+1}|\bigr),$$
using zero for a missing boundary term, and record the old value in $D^B$.
A one-by-one diagonal pair at $k$ is isolated when $H_{k,k-1}=0$ and
$H_{k+1,k}=0$, omitting a boundary entry when $k=a$ or $k=b$. If it has
$T_{k,k}=0$ and $H_{k,k}\ne0$, report an infinite eigenvalue and deflate it
from the active block. If the isolated diagonal pair is $(0,0)$, return
`singular-pencil-suspected` without assigning an eigenvalue.

3. To move a non-isolated zero $T_{k,k}$ to the top of its active block, for
$j=k-1,k-2,\ldots,a$ apply a right Givens factor on columns $j,j+1$ that
zeros $T_{j,j}$, then, when $j+2\le b$, a left Givens factor on rows
$j+1,j+2$ that zeros the resulting bulge $H_{j+2,j}$. Finally, when $a<b$,
apply a left Givens factor on rows $a,a+1$ to zero $H_{a+1,a}$. Record all rounded update
residuals. If this isolates $(H_{a,a},T_{a,a})=(h,0)$ with $h\ne0$, report
the infinite eigenvalue and remove the first row/column from the active block.

sweep, choose the homogeneous shift $[\alpha:\beta]=[H_{b,b}:T_{b,b}]$ if this pair is nonzero and
$T_{b,b}\ne0$; if $T_{b,b}=0$, use $[0:1]$. Form
$$x=(\beta H_{a:b,a:b}-\alpha T_{a:b,a:b})e_1.$$

second. Apply a right Givens factor to columns $1,2$ to restore triangularity
of $T$. For $j=2,\ldots,b-a$, alternate a left Givens factor on rows $j,j+1$
to zero the current Hessenberg bulge and a right Givens factor on columns

triangle inequality. The residual certificate is inconclusive if the lemma's

terminates with a declared status. After each successful initialization or
QZ/infinite-deflation sweep, the stored pair is Hessenberg-triangular, except

factor record and local update residuals, the returned pair $(S,T)$ satisfies
$$S=Q^*(A+\Delta_A)Z,\qquad T=Q^*(B+\Delta_B)Z,$$

deflation perturbation pair. This proposition gives no bound on its size.

Let $n\ge1$, $m\ge0$, $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and
$A,B\in\mathbb F^{n\times n}$. Put $A_0=A$, $B_0=B$. For
$j=1,\ldots,m$, suppose exact unitary/orthogonal factors $Q_j,Z_j$ and local
arithmetic/deflation perturbations satisfy
$$A_j=Q_j^*(A_{j-1}+E_j^A+D_j^A)Z_j,$$
$$B_j=Q_j^*(B_{j-1}+E_j^B+D_j^B)Z_j.$$
Then with $Q=Q_1\cdots Q_m$ and $Z=Z_1\cdots Z_m$ (empty products are $I_n$)
there are perturbations
$\Delta_A,\Delta_B$ such that
$$A_m=Q^*(A+\Delta_A)Z,\qquad B_m=Q^*(B+\Delta_B)Z,$$
and
$$\sqrt{\|\Delta_A\|_F^2+\|\Delta_B\|_F^2} \le\sum_{j=1}^m\left( \sqrt{\|E_j^A\|_F^2+\|E_j^B\|_F^2} +\sqrt{\|D_j^A\|_F^2+\|D_j^B\|_F^2}\right).$$

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$, and
let $\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_r>0$ be the positive singular values of
$A$, where $r=\operatorname{rank}A$; write $\sigma_1=0$ when $r=0$.

1. **Spectral formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_2=\sigma_1$, where $\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ is
   the operator norm of [[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]].
2. **Frobenius formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_F=\bigl(\sigma_1^{2}+\cdots+\sigma_r^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$.
3. **Unitary invariance.** For every unitary $U\in M_m(\mathbb F)$ and
   $V\in M_n(\mathbb F)$ (over $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$: orthogonal matrices),
   $$\lVert UAV\rVert_2=\lVert A\rVert_2,\qquad \lVert UAV\rVert_F=\lVert A\rVert_F.$$
4. **Sharp rank comparison.**
   $$\lVert A\rVert_2\;\le\;\lVert A\rVert_F\;\le\;\sqrt{r}\,\lVert A\rVert_2.$$
   The lower inequality is an equality exactly when $r\le 1$; the upper
   inequality is an equality exactly when $\sigma_1=\cdots=\sigma_r$, that is,

   $\lVert A\rVert_F\le\sqrt{\min(m,n)}\,\lVert A\rVert_2$.

$$g_r=\frac{ru}{1-ru},\quad e_r=(1+u)^{r/2+3}-1,\quad d_r=e_r+u(2+e_r),\quad a_r=\frac{1+u}{(1-u)^r}-1,$$
$$c_r=2\bigl((1+a_r)(1+u)^2(1+g_r)-1\bigr),\qquad \kappa_r=\max\{e_r+8d_r,(1+u)c_r+3u\}.$$
There is an exact orthogonal $H$, the identity when $x=0$ and $H(v)=I-2vv^T/(v^Tv)$ otherwise, and a perturbation $E$ such that
$$H(C+E)=C_+,\qquad \|E\|_F\le\kappa_r\|C\|_F.$$
The constants increase with $r$ and are $O(ru)$ for fixed $r$ as $u\to0$. The column overwrite is included. For successful application of the same stored $(v,\widehat\tau)$ to a separate block $Y$ without an annihilation overwrite, the discrepancy from $H(v)Y$ is at most $((1+u)c_r+3u)\|Y\|_F$.

Suppose the finite reduction returns a product $Q$ of exact unitary reflector representatives and computed factor $\widehat T$, after any finite successful prefix or completed run. Index all Hessenberg and QR updates by $j$, including each pure deflation as an identity-transform stage with zero arithmetic coefficient. Suppose
$$\widehat H_j=P_j^*(\widehat H_{j-1}+E_j+D_j)P_j,\qquad \|E_j\|_F\le\alpha_j\|\widehat H_{j-1}\|_F,$$
where $D_j$ records the exact deflation zero writes and each $P_j$ is the exact stored-vector representative. Then
$$\widehat T=Q^*(A+\Delta)Q,\qquad \|\Delta\|_F\le\sum_j\alpha_j\|\widehat H_{j-1}\|_F+\sum_j\|D_j\|_F.$$

coefficients when $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$. The pencil is **regular** if $f$ is
not the zero polynomial; otherwise it is **singular**.

For $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb C$ not both zero, put
$$p(\alpha,\beta)=\det(\beta A-\alpha B).$$
A **homogeneous generalized eigenvalue pair** is an equivalence class of such
pairs satisfying $p(\alpha,\beta)=0$, where $(\alpha,\beta)$ and
$(c\alpha,c\beta)$ represent the same pair for every $c\in\mathbb C\setminus
\{0\}$. If $\beta\ne0$, the associated finite generalized eigenvalue is
$\lambda=\alpha/\beta$; if $\beta=0$, the pair is an infinite generalized
eigenvalue. The pair $(0,0)$ is never an eigenvalue pair.
Write $\sigma(A,B)$ for the set of finite ratios $\alpha/\beta$ among these
homogeneous eigenvalue pairs.
